Dekker attended [[Sheboygan Lutheran High School]] in [[Sheboygan, Wisconsin|Sheboygan]], [[Wisconsin]]. Dekker is a very highly rated [[NBA]] draft prospect.{{cite web|last=Ogden|first=Maxwell|title=2014 NBA Mock Draft: Early Projections for entire 1st Round|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1687393-2014-nba-mock-draft-early-projections-for-entire-1st-round|publisher=Bleacher Report|accessdate=13 November 2013}}[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Sam-Dekker-6438/ Draft Express 2014 NBA Draft Rankings] ==High school career== Dekker was named Wisconsin Gatorade Player of the Year following his senior season. He was also named 2012 [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]], [[Associated Press|AP]] first team all-state and Wisconsin Basketball Coaches' Association's Mr. Basketball Award. He led [[Sheboygan Lutheran High School|Sheboygan Lutheran]] to the school's first ever [[Wisconsin Interscholastic Athletic Association|WIAA]] state title. Dekker scored 40 points in the title game including the game winning three point shot with two seconds left.{{cite web|title=Sam Dekker Wisconsin Badgers profile|url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/sam_dekker_801183.html|publisher=uwbadgers.com|accessdate=March 28, 2015}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|collapse=no|year=2012}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Sam Dekker | position = SF | hometown = Sheboygan, WI | highschool = Sheboygan Lutheran | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 195 | 40 = | commitdate = 6/15/2010 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | grayshirt = }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2012 | rivals ref title = 2012 Wisconsin Commitments | scout ref title = Men's Basketball Recruiting | espn ref title = ESPN- Wisconsin Badgers Men's Basketball Recruiting | espn schoolid = | scout overall = 4 ([[Small forward|SF]]) | rivals overall = 3 (SF) | espn overall = 4 (SF) | accessdate = December 10, 2011 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===Freshman season=== Dekker played in 35 games (3 starts) as a freshman on the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]]. He is one of only four true freshman to start under [[Bo Ryan]] joining [[Devin Harris]], [[Alando Tucker]] and Josh Gasser. He earned Big Ten All-Freshman team recognition as well as honorable mention All-Big Ten honors. He was also two-time Big Ten Freshman of the Week (Jan. 14 and March 4, 2013). Dekker scored a season high 19 points against [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] on November 24, 2012 and [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] on February 26, 2013. ===Sophomore season=== Before the season, Dekker was named to the [[Wooden Award]] and [[Naismith Trophy]] watch lists.[http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112113aaa.html Dekker named to Watch Lists] At the conclusion of the regular season, Dekker was named to the Second Team All-Big Ten by the coaches and Third Team All-Big Ten by the media.{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031014aag.html|title=Big Ten Announces 2014 Men's Basketball Postseason Honors: Michigan's Stauskas named Big Ten Player of the Year|accessdate=2014-03-10|date=2014-03-10|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}} ===Junior season=== Before the season, Dekker was named to the Wooden Award and Naismith Trophy watch lists. At the conclusion of the regular season, Dekker was named to the Second Team All-Big Ten by the coaches and by the media. He was also named West Regional Most Outstanding Player during the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. The Badgers finished second in the NCAA tournament before losing to Duke in the finals. A week later, Dekker decided to forgo his senior season, dropping out of the University of Wisconsin–Madison, and declare himself eligible for the NBA draft.{{cite news|title=Wisconsin's Sam Dekker headed to NBA draft|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2015/04/10/sam-dekker-wisconsin-nba-draft/25575051/|accessdate=11 April 2015|publisher=USA Today|date=April 10, 2015}} ==International career== In the summer of 2012, Dekker was on the under-18 United States national team that defeated Brazil for the gold medal in the [[FIBA]] Americas championship. He was limited due to an injury.{{cite news|last1=Markus|first1=Don|title=Against old teammate, Terps' Jake Layman seeks to show he
